title: Job, Chapter 31 (Leningrad Codex)
source: Leningrad Codex folios (Internet Archive, WSRP photographs) + tanach.us LC folio index + UXLC Hebrew + KJV
description: Job 31 on folios 405v, 406r of the Leningrad Codex (1008 AD), the oldest complete Hebrew Bible. Hebrew from the UXLC transcription of this manuscript; English KJV.
introduction:
Job chapter 31 from the Leningrad Codex (Codex Leningradensis, National Library of Russia, Firkovich EBP. I B 19a), copied in Cairo by Samuel ben Jacob and dated 1008/1009 AD, the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible and the base text of the Biblia Hebraica editions. This chapter stands on folios 405v, 406r.

This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: the specific folio side(s) carrying each section's verses, from the full-colour West Semitic Research Project photographs of the codex as redistributed on Internet Archive (item Leningrad_Codex_Color_Images, marked Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0). Folio-to-verse ranges come from the tanach.us LC folio index, which was derived from the West Semitic Research Project's published index; each section links only to the page(s) whose recorded verse range contains its verses.
  2. Original text: the verbatim Hebrew of this manuscript in the Unicode/XML Leningrad Codex (UXLC 2.5 build 27.6, tanach.us), a transcription of Firkovich B 19a with vowels and cantillation, released without restriction on the biblical text.
  3. English translation: the King James Version (1611, public domain), retrieved verbatim from bolls.life (KJV text, Strong's numbers stripped).
translator_notes: Ketiv/Qere: where the scribe wrote one form (ketiv) but the Masoretes read another (qere), the consonantal ketiv is given first and the vocalised qere follows in square brackets. פ and ס mark the open and closed paragraph breaks visible as gaps in the manuscript columns.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>בְּ֭רִית כָּרַ֣תִּי לְעֵינָ֑י וּמָ֥ה אֶ֝תְבּוֹנֵ֗ן עַל־בְּתוּלָֽה׃ <sup>2</sup>וּמֶ֤ה ׀ חֵ֣לֶק אֱל֣וֹהַּ מִמָּ֑עַל וְֽנַחֲלַ֥ת שַׁ֝דַּ֗י מִמְּרֹמִֽים׃ <sup>3</sup>הֲלֹא־אֵ֥יד לְעַוָּ֑ל וְ֝נֵ֗כֶר לְפֹ֣עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃ <sup>4</sup>הֲלֹא־ה֭וּא יִרְאֶ֣ה דְרָכָ֑י וְֽכָל־צְעָדַ֥י יִסְפּֽוֹר׃ <sup>5</sup>אִם־הָלַ֥כְתִּי עִם־שָׁ֑וְא וַתַּ֖חַשׁ עַל־מִרְמָ֣ה רַגְלֽ͏ִי׃ <sup>6</sup>יִשְׁקְלֵ֥נִי בְמֹאזְנֵי־צֶ֑דֶק וְיֵדַ֥ע אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַּ תֻּמָּתִֽי׃ <sup>7</sup>אִ֥ם תִּטֶּ֣ה אַשֻּׁרִי֮ מִנִּ֢י הַ֫דָּ֥רֶךְ וְאַחַ֣ר עֵ֭ינַי הָלַ֣ךְ לִבִּ֑י וּ֝בְכַפַּ֗י דָּ֣בַק מֻאוּֽם׃ פ <sup>8</sup>אֶ֭זְרְעָה וְאַחֵ֣ר יֹאכֵ֑ל וְֽצֶאֱצָאַ֥י יְשֹׁרָֽשׁוּ׃
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid? <sup>2</sup>For what portion of God is there from above? and what inheritance of the Almighty from on high? <sup>3</sup>Is not destruction to the wicked? and a strange punishment to the workers of iniquity? <sup>4</sup>Doth not he see my ways, and count all my steps? <sup>5</sup>If I have walked with vanity, or if my foot hath hasted to deceit; <sup>6</sup>Let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know mine integrity. <sup>7</sup>If my step hath turned out of the way, and mine heart walked after mine eyes, and if any blot hath cleaved to mine hands; <sup>8</sup>Then let me sow, and let another eat; yea, let my offspring be rooted out.

translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>אִם־נִפְתָּ֣ה לִ֭בִּי עַל־אִשָּׁ֑ה וְעַל־פֶּ֖תַח רֵעִ֣י אָרָֽבְתִּי׃ <sup>10</sup>תִּטְחַ֣ן לְאַחֵ֣ר אִשְׁתִּ֑י וְ֝עָלֶ֗יהָ יִכְרְע֥וּן אֲחֵרִֽין׃ <sup>11</sup>כִּי־הוא [הִ֥יא] זִמָּ֑ה והיא [וְ֝ה֗וּא] עָוֺ֥ן פְּלִילִֽים׃ <sup>12</sup>כִּ֤י אֵ֣שׁ הִ֭יא עַד־אֲבַדּ֣וֹן תֹּאכֵ֑ל וּֽבְכָל־תְּב֖וּאָתִ֣י תְשָׁרֵֽשׁ׃ <sup>13</sup>אִם־אֶמְאַ֗ס מִשְׁפַּ֣ט עַ֭בְדִּי וַאֲמָתִ֑י בְּ֝רִבָ֗ם עִמָּדִֽי׃ <sup>14</sup>וּמָ֣ה אֶֽ֭עֱשֶׂה כִּֽי־יָק֣וּם אֵ֑ל וְכִֽי־יִ֝פְקֹ֗ד מָ֣ה אֲשִׁיבֶֽנּוּ׃ <sup>15</sup>הֲ‍ֽ֝לֹא־בַ֭בֶּטֶן עֹשֵׂ֣נִי עָשָׂ֑הוּ וַ֝יְכֻנֶ֗נּוּ בָּרֶ֥חֶם אֶחָֽד׃ <sup>16</sup>אִם־אֶ֭מְנַע מֵחֵ֣פֶץ דַּלִּ֑ים וְעֵינֵ֖י אַלְמָנָ֣ה אֲכַלֶּֽה׃
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>If mine heart have been deceived by a woman, or if I have laid wait at my neighbour's door; <sup>10</sup>Then let my wife grind unto another, and let others bow down upon her. <sup>11</sup>For this is an heinous crime; yea, it is an iniquity to be punished by the judges. <sup>12</sup>For it is a fire that consumeth to destruction, and would root out all mine increase. <sup>13</sup>If I did despise the cause of my manservant or of my maidservant, when they contended with me; <sup>14</sup>What then shall I do when God riseth up? and when he visiteth, what shall I answer him? <sup>15</sup>Did not he that made me in the womb make him? and did not one fashion us in the womb? <sup>16</sup>If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail;

translation.original_text: <sup>17</sup>וְאֹכַ֣ל פִּתִּ֣י לְבַדִּ֑י וְלֹא־אָכַ֖ל יָת֣וֹם מִמֶּֽנָּה׃ <sup>18</sup>כִּ֣י מִ֭נְּעוּרַי גְּדֵלַ֣נִי כְאָ֑ב וּמִבֶּ֖טֶן אִמִּ֣י אַנְחֶֽנָּה׃ <sup>19</sup>אִם־אֶרְאֶ֣ה א֖וֹבֵד מִבְּלִ֣י לְב֑וּשׁ וְאֵ֥ין כְּ֝ס֗וּת לָאֶבְיֽוֹן׃ <sup>20</sup>אִם־לֹ֣א בֵרֲכ֣וּנִי חלצו [חֲלָצָ֑יו] וּמִגֵּ֥ז כְּ֝בָשַׂי יִתְחַמָּֽם׃ <sup>21</sup>אִם־הֲנִיפ֣וֹתִי עַל־יָת֣וֹם יָדִ֑י כִּֽי־אֶרְאֶ֥ה בַ֝שַּׁ֗עַר עֶזְרָתִֽי׃ <sup>22</sup>כְּ֭תֵפִי מִשִּׁכְמָ֣ה תִפּ֑וֹל וְ֝אֶזְרֹעִ֗י מִקָּנָ֥ה תִשָּׁבֵֽר׃ <sup>23</sup>כִּ֤י פַ֣חַד אֵ֭לַי אֵ֣יד אֵ֑ל וּ֝מִשְּׂאֵת֗וֹ לֹ֣א אוּכָֽל׃ <sup>24</sup>אִם־שַׂ֣מְתִּי זָהָ֣ב כִּסְלִ֑י וְ֝לַכֶּ֗תֶם אָמַ֥רְתִּי מִבְטַחִֽי׃
translation.text: <sup>17</sup>Or have eaten my morsel myself alone, and the fatherless hath not eaten thereof; <sup>18</sup>(For from my youth he was brought up with me, as with a father, and I have guided her from my mother's womb;) <sup>19</sup>If I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or any poor without covering; <sup>20</sup>If his loins have not blessed me, and if he were not warmed with the fleece of my sheep; <sup>21</sup>If I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, when I saw my help in the gate: <sup>22</sup>Then let mine arm fall from my shoulder blade, and mine arm be broken from the bone. <sup>23</sup>For destruction from God was a terror to me, and by reason of his highness I could not endure. <sup>24</sup>If I have made gold my hope, or have said to the fine gold, Thou art my confidence;

translation.original_text: <sup>25</sup>אִם־אֶ֭שְׂמַח כִּי־רַ֣ב חֵילִ֑י וְכִֽי־כַ֝בִּ֗יר מָצְאָ֥ה יָדִֽי׃ <sup>26</sup>אִם־אֶרְאֶ֣ה א֖וֹר כִּ֣י יָהֵ֑ל וְ֝יָרֵ֗חַ יָקָ֥ר הֹלֵֽךְ׃ <sup>27</sup>וַיִּ֣פְתְּ בַּסֵּ֣תֶר לִבִּ֑י וַתִּשַּׁ֖ק יָדִ֣י לְפִֽי׃ <sup>28</sup>גַּם־ה֖וּא עָוֺ֣ן פְּלִילִ֑י כִּֽי־כִחַ֖שְׁתִּי לָאֵ֣ל מִמָּֽעַל׃ <sup>29</sup>אִם־אֶ֭שְׂמַח בְּפִ֣יד מְשַׂנְאִ֑י וְ֝הִתְעֹרַ֗רְתִּי כִּֽי־מְצָ֥אוֹ רָֽע׃ <sup>30</sup>וְלֹא־נָתַ֣תִּי לַחֲטֹ֣א חִכִּ֑י לִשְׁאֹ֖ל בְּאָלָ֣ה נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃ <sup>31</sup>אִם־לֹ֣א אָ֭מְרוּ מְתֵ֣י אָהֳלִ֑י מִֽי־יִתֵּ֥ן מִ֝בְּשָׂר֗וֹ לֹ֣א נִשְׂבָּֽע׃ <sup>32</sup>בַּ֭חוּץ לֹא־יָלִ֣ין גֵּ֑ר דְּ֝לָתַ֗י לָאֹ֥רַח אֶפְתָּֽח׃
translation.text: <sup>25</sup>If I rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because mine hand had gotten much; <sup>26</sup>If I beheld the sun when it shined, or the moon walking in brightness; <sup>27</sup>And my heart hath been secretly enticed, or my mouth hath kissed my hand: <sup>28</sup>This also were an iniquity to be punished by the judge: for I should have denied the God that is above. <sup>29</sup>If I rejoiced at the destruction of him that hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him: <sup>30</sup>Neither have I suffered my mouth to sin by wishing a curse to his soul. <sup>31</sup>If the men of my tabernacle said not, Oh that we had of his flesh! we cannot be satisfied. <sup>32</sup>The stranger did not lodge in the street: but I opened my doors to the traveller.

translation.original_text: <sup>33</sup>אִם־כִּסִּ֣יתִי כְאָדָ֣ם פְּשָׁעָ֑י לִטְמ֖וֹן בְּחֻבִּ֣י עֲוֺֽנִי׃ <sup>34</sup>כִּ֤י אֶֽעֱר֨וֹץ ׀ הָ֘מ֤וֹן רַבָּ֗ה וּבוּז־מִשְׁפָּח֥וֹת יְחִתֵּ֑נִי וָ֝אֶדֹּ֗ם לֹא־אֵ֥צֵא פָֽתַח׃ <sup>35</sup>מִ֤י יִתֶּן־לִ֨י ׀ שֹׁ֘מֵ֤עַֽ לִ֗י הֶן־תָּ֭וִי שַׁדַּ֣י יַעֲנֵ֑נִי וְסֵ֥פֶר כָּ֝תַ֗ב אִ֣ישׁ רִיבִֽי׃ <sup>36</sup>אִם־לֹ֣א עַל־שִׁ֭כְמִי אֶשָּׂאֶ֑נּוּ אֶֽעֶנְדֶ֖נּוּ עֲטָר֣וֹת לִֽי׃ <sup>37</sup>מִסְפַּ֣ר צְ֭עָדַי אַגִּידֶ֑נּוּ כְּמוֹ־נָ֝גִ֗יד אֲקָרֲבֶֽנּוּ׃ <sup>38</sup>אִם־עָ֭לַי אַדְמָתִ֣י תִזְעָ֑ק וְ֝יַ֗חַד תְּלָמֶ֥יהָ יִבְכָּיֽוּן׃ <sup>39</sup>אִם־כֹּ֭חָהּ אָכַ֣לְתִּי בְלִי־כָ֑סֶף וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ בְּעָלֶ֣יהָ הִפָּֽחְתִּי׃ <sup>40</sup>תַּ֤חַת חִטָּ֨ה ׀ יֵ֥צֵא ח֗וֹחַ וְתַֽחַת־שְׂעֹרָ֥ה בָאְשָׁ֑ה תַּ֝֗מּוּ דִּבְרֵ֥י אִיּֽוֹב׃ פ
translation.text: <sup>33</sup>If I covered my transgressions as Adam, by hiding mine iniquity in my bosom: <sup>34</sup>Did I fear a great multitude, or did the contempt of families terrify me, that I kept silence, and went not out of the door? <sup>35</sup>Oh that one would hear me! behold, my desire is, that the Almighty would answer me, and that mine adversary had written a book. <sup>36</sup>Surely I would take it upon my shoulder, and bind it as a crown to me. <sup>37</sup>I would declare unto him the number of my steps; as a prince would I go near unto him. <sup>38</sup>If my land cry against me, or that the furrows likewise thereof complain; <sup>39</sup>If I have eaten the fruits thereof without money, or have caused the owners thereof to lose their life: <sup>40</sup>Let thistles grow instead of wheat, and cockle instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.
